      "category": "perf",
      "title": "All app-store imports are started eagerly, not lazily",
      "body": "The appStore object initializes every entry with import(...) at module load. Importing appStore therefore starts loading every app chunk, even if only one integration is used. This defeats much of the benefit of async imports and can increase startup/network cost. It also creates many promises that may never be awaited; if one dynamic import fails and that app is never used, the rejection may become unhandled. A lazy getter or function that imports only the requested app would be safer."

      "body": "getCalendar now awaits appStore[...] but does not catch errors from the dynamic import. Previously an unknown or unavailable calendar type could return null after a warning; now a rejected import throws. Callers such as CalendarManager.getCachedResults use Promise.all over getCalendar, so one broken app can fail all calendar availability requests. Wrap the import lookup in try/catch and return null, or otherwise handle the failure."
    },

      "severity": "high",

      "body": "bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) starts asynchronous getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting operations, but Array.prototype.forEach does not wait for the callbacks' promises. The surrounding try/catch will not catch rejections, and Reschedule can send the reschedule email and return before the external events are deleted. Use Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)) or a for...of loop with await."

Use Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)) or a for...of loop with await."

      "body": "bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) performs awaited getCalendar and returns deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises, but forEach ignores those promises. The mutation can complete, send emails, and call webhooks before external calendar/video events are deleted, and any deletion failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Use Promise.all or a for...of loop and await the deletions."
    },

      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Async forEach can leave apiDeletes unpopulated and unawaited",
      "body": "The recurring-calendar cancellation branch uses .forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(...) }). Because forEach does not await async callbacks, later code may reach await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) before apiDeletes is fully populated, so calendar deletions may not be awaited or may be skipped. Errors from those async callbacks are also unhandled. Use a for...of loop or collect promises with map and Promise.all."

findings.title: All app-store imports are started eagerly, not lazily
findings.body: The appStore object initializes every entry with import(...) at module load. Importing appStore therefore starts loading every app chunk, even if only one integration is used. This defeats much of the benefit of async imports and can increase startup/network cost. It also creates many promises that may never be awaited; if one dynamic import fails and that app is never used, the rejection may become unhandled. A lazy getter or function that imports only the requested app would be safer.

findings.title: Dynamic import failures in getCalendar reject instead of returning null
findings.body: getCalendar now awaits appStore[...] but does not catch errors from the dynamic import. Previously an unknown or unavailable calendar type could return null after a warning; now a rejected import throws. Callers such as CalendarManager.getCachedResults use Promise.all over getCalendar, so one broken app can fail all calendar availability requests. Wrap the import lookup in try/catch and return null, or otherwise handle the failure.

findings.title: Async forEach does not await calendar/video deletions
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) starts asynchronous getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting operations, but Array.prototype.forEach does not wait for the callbacks' promises. The surrounding try/catch will not catch rejections, and Reschedule can send the reschedule email and return before the external events are deleted. Use Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)) or a for...of loop with await.

findings.title: Async forEach does not await calendar/video deletions
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) starts asynchronous getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting operations, but Array.prototype.forEach does not wait for the callbacks' promises. The surrounding try/catch will not catch rejections, and Reschedule can send the reschedule email and return before the external events are deleted. Use Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...)) or a for...of loop with await.

findings.title: Reschedule mutation fires calendar/video deletions without awaiting them
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) performs awaited getCalendar and returns deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises, but forEach ignores those promises. The mutation can complete, send emails, and call webhooks before external calendar/video events are deleted, and any deletion failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Use Promise.all or a for...of loop and await the deletions.

findings.title: Async forEach can leave apiDeletes unpopulated and unawaited
findings.body: The recurring-calendar cancellation branch uses .forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(...) }). Because forEach does not await async callbacks, later code may reach await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) before apiDeletes is fully populated, so calendar deletions may not be awaited or may be skipped. Errors from those async callbacks are also unhandled. Use a for...of loop or collect promises with map and Promise.all.

findings.title: Awaiting the apiDeletes array does not await its promises
findings.body: In the paid cancellation path, await apiDeletes; awaits the array object, not the promises it may contain. The handler can return before calendar/video deletion promises settle, and rejections from those promises may become unhandled. It should be await Promise.all(apiDeletes), after ensuring apiDeletes is fully populated.
